E1.evidence: Public GitHub issue ros-controls/ros2_control#1179 (opened 2023-11-24, labelled bug, closed 2025-05-19 by the stale bot) with a reproducer and logs. Reporter: "Calling the service **/controller_manager/switch_controller** return always true even if it could not switch the controllers." Reproducer: "ros2 service call /controller_manager/switch_controller controller_manager_msgs/srv/SwitchController \"{start_controllers: [\"dummy_controller\"]}\"" giving "controller_manager_msgs.srv.SwitchController_Response(ok=True)" while the controller manager logs an error. Re-reproduced on Humble at the maintainer's request (2024-01-07): "[controller_manager]: Could not 'activate' controller with name 'dummy_controller' because no controller with this name exists" / "[controller_manager]: Empty activate and deactivate list, not requesting switch" / "But the service response is Ok". Maintainers engage with the behaviour (saikishor: "Please try with the `strictness` set to `STRICT` when sending the service request. I think it should respond with false."; christophfroehlich: "Hint: the problem with `STRICT` is, that it does return false also if the controller exists but is already in the desired state."; fmauch: "When switching a controller passes the `prepare_switch` method in the HW interface but causes a conflict in the resource manager, the service still returns `ok=True`."). No fix is linked to the issue.

E2.evidence: Step 1: the controller_manager node (package controller_manager, ros-controls/ros2_control), which serves /controller_manager/switch_controller, and the service client process `ros2 service call` (package ros2service, ros2/ros2cli), which the reporter uses to send the request; the response text "controller_manager_msgs.srv.SwitchController_Response(ok=True)" is the output of ros2service's call verb ("print('response:\n%r\n' % future.result())"). Two processes interacting only through a ROS 2 service. Step 2: the defect is the value of the response field ok, which crosses the boundary: the client is told ok=True although the requested switch was not performed (the controller manager logged "Could not 'activate' controller with name 'dummy_controller' because no controller with this name exists" and "Empty activate and deactivate list, not requesting switch"). A wrong value crossing the boundary is an interface failure even though any fix is inside the provider. Step 3: no name binding involved. Step 4: no build or packaging change. Step 5: no firmware. Step 6: eligible; interface kind: service (/controller_manager/switch_controller, type controller_manager_msgs/srv/SwitchController).

E3.evidence: PAIR: the client's request is consumed by the controller manager and the controller manager's response (field ok) is consumed by the client; the failure was observed in this request/response exchange ("response:\ncontroller_manager_msgs.srv.SwitchController_Response(ok=True)"). No UPGRADE, CONCURRENT or SWITCH relation between these two units is documented (the resource conflict between two controllers that fmauch describes is a different composition; see notes).

E4.evidence: Observed wrong data in the response: expected "ok = False" ("The response expected should be ok = False but the ok is equals to true"), observed "controller_manager_msgs.srv.SwitchController_Response(ok=True)" on Foxy and again on Humble ("I  tested in humble and appears the same problem"). Code-level confirmation at the Humble revision: switch_controller() returns OK on the empty-list path ("RCLCPP_INFO(get_logger(), \"Empty activate and deactivate list, not requesting switch\"); clear_requests(); return controller_interface::return_type::OK;") and the service callback sets "response->ok = switch_controller(...) == controller_interface::return_type::OK;".

failed_conditions.quote: Calling the service **/controller_manager/switch_controller** return always true even if it could not switch the controllers.

[controller_manager]: Could not 'activate' controller with name 'dummy_controller' because no controller with this name exists      
[controller_manager]: Empty activate and deactivate list, not requesting switch

loudness_evidence: The controller manager emits a diagnostic at activation time for the refused switch: on Humble "[controller_manager]: Could not 'activate' controller with name 'dummy_controller' because no controller with this name exists" (https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/issues/1179#issuecomment-1880057833); in the original Foxy report a resource-manager claim error, "Resource conflict for controller 'dummy_controller'. Command interface 'XXXX' is already claimed." (https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/issues/1179). The diagnostic appears only in the provider's log; the service response delivered to the client signals success ("controller_manager_msgs.srv.SwitchController_Response(ok=True)"), so the client side sees no diagnostic.

resolution.summary: Client-side workaround recommended by a maintainer: send the request with strictness = STRICT (2) instead of the default 0 (treated as BEST_EFFORT). At revision 945d64ed the controller manager then returns ERROR for a controller name that does not exist ("RCLCPP_ERROR(get_logger(), \"Aborting, no controller is switched! ('STRICT' switch)\"); return controller_interface::return_type::ERROR;"), so the response carries ok=false. No code change to either unit.
resolution.evidence: saikishor (2024-01-26): "Please try with the `strictness` set to `STRICT` when sending the service request. I think it should respond with false." (https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/issues/1179#issuecomment-1911700097). christophfroehlich (2024-01-26): "Hint: the problem with `STRICT` is, that it does return false also if the controller exists but is already in the desired state." (https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/issues/1179#issuecomment-1912400524). The reporter never confirms the workaround, and fmauch (2024-11-08) shows it does not cover a resource-manager conflict: "while the first controller being active, activate the second controller through the controller switch service **with strictness STRICT**." ... "The service response will contain `ok=True`." (https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/issues/1179#issuecomment-2464683564). Code at the broken revision: https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/blob/945d64ed3640e8fcda6050958e020ca17ef1eb8b/controller_manager/src/controller_manager.cpp#L800-L806 (STRICT path returns ERROR; BEST_EFFORT only warns), #L1068-L1073 (empty request lists return OK), #L1741-L1743 (response->ok set from the return value). The issue was closed by the stale bot on 2025-05-19 without a linked fix.

notes: Composition choice: the reporter's reproduced problem is the service exchange between a `ros2 service call` client and the controller manager (wrong ok in the response), so that composition is specified. Other compositions documented in the thread: (a) two controllers claiming the same command interface at the same time, which the resource manager refuses at activation (fmauch, 2024-11-08: "define two controllers claiming the same interface, e.g. all joints' position interface", "... [controller_manager]: Resource conflict for controller [...]. Comand interface 'jointXYZ/position' is already claimed."; the reporter's Foxy log also shows "Resource conflict for controller 'dummy_controller'. Command interface 'XXXX' is already claimed."), a CONCURRENT composition with an exclusive_resource_conflict on the joint command interface, loud (resource-manager claim error) but, per fmauch, also answered with ok=True even under STRICT; (b) the hardware interface's prepare_switch versus the resource manager's claim check, mentioned by fmauch. Condition 2 records the runtime's refusal of the request itself (the reporter deliberately named a controller that does not exist), as the instructions ask for enforced refusals within the composition; it is the trigger, not a defect of either unit. Sides in the inventory follow data flow: request fields are provided by the client and consumed by the controller manager; the response field ok is provided by the controller manager and consumed by the client. The Humble reproduction used `ros2_control_demo_example_1 rrbot.launch.py` from ros-controls/ros2_control_demos (humble head on 2024-01-07: 705f9cccd56344b37d097b7cebfffa4db1101ab0); the demo's controllers and hardware are not units of the specified composition. Mechanism at 945d64ed: with strictness 0 the controller manager defaults to BEST_EFFORT ("Defaulting to ::BEST_EFFORT"), a non-existent name is dropped with a WARN, the activate list becomes empty and switch_controller() returns OK; for a controller that exists but fails to claim its command interfaces, activate_controllers() logs "Resource conflict for controller '%s'. Command interface '%s' is already claimed." (line 1364), skips the controller (continue), sets switch_params_.do_switch = false (line 1433), and switch_controller() still returns OK (line 1141). Later provider-side changes not linked to this issue: PR #1941 (master, merged 2024-12-21, merge commit 038a05f512a58e9b23f9d282395c992fde3e6c36) and its humble backport PR #1968 (merged 2024-12-22, merge commit 4c58cda427b4e4f32a153fd8f11c39a91001941b) make switch_controller() return ERROR when a requested controller is not active after the switch ("Could not activate controller : '%s'"), so a resource-conflict activation failure now yields ok=false; the PR body shows exactly the resource-conflict scenario. This does not change the BEST_EFFORT non-existent-name path, which still returns OK on the current humble branch ("Empty activate and deactivate list, not requesting switch"). PR #2088 (master only, merged 2025-03-13, merge commit 582fbe187afd00f5d3b5c2456a20554ed40bcdb5) adds a `string message` field to the SwitchController response; the humble SwitchController.srv response is still only `bool ok`. These are recorded as context, not as the resolution of this case. Unknowns: whether the reporter used binary packages or a source build (revisions are branch heads on the reproduction dates); the exact command used in the Humble retest (only the result is shown); the reporter's own environment for the original Foxy run beyond "Ubuntu 20.04 / Foxy".
